nodes.question: What technology is used for scanning in the ZEISS Scout-and-Scan system?
nodes.answer: The ZEISS Scout-and-Scan technology allows for low-resolution, large FOV scans followed by high-resolution scans of regions of interest.
nodes.paragraph: The ZEISS Scout-and-Scan technology canallow for a low-resolution, large FOV scan to rst be conducted, and then regions of interest can be zoomed-in on and a high-resolution scan can betaken of a sub-volume of the sample to reveal more detail. The X-ray source applies a voltage, which can vary from 30 to 160 kVp, to a tungsten target to produce a Bremsstrahlung X-ray spectrum in a cone-beam geometry with maximum energies thatcan range from 30 to 160 keV. In September 2023, this instrument was upgraded to the ZEISS Xradia 620 Versa, shown in Fig. 1, which provided an upgraded source, increasing the X-ray source powerfrom 10 to 25 W, while keeping the X-ray energy range the same. This upgrade reduces imaging time by approximately a factor of 2 while also improvingthe detection statistics for high-resolution imaging. Computational Resources The Xradia 620 Versa is equipped with a work- station containing a Xeon processor clocked at 2.20 GHz, which helps with data collection and perform preliminary image reconstruction, a pro-cess which converts the 2D radiographs to 3Dvolumetric data. This machine has the ZEISS Scout-and-Scan Control System Reconstructor soft- ware installed in it which can perform preliminaryreconstructions from radiographic datasets.
